record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Is every quasi Riemann surface Q isomorphic to the space D_int_0(Σ) of integral 0-currents on some ordinary two-dimensional conformal space Σ with the same Jacobian, and if so how can that isomorphism be constructed concretely?

evidence.quote: Conjecturally, every quasi Riemann surface Q is isomorphic to D_int_0(Σ) for Σ the 2d conformal space with the same Jacobian as Q, the Jacobian being the complex torus made from the homology in the middle dimension.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A quasi Riemann surface is a structure Q (in the sense of Friedan) that abstracts the properties of spaces of integral 0-currents on a Riemann surface: it carries a commutative associative addition with cancellation, a distinguished asymptotic cone of "effective" elements, a complete weak metric, and additional structure (integral j-currents for j = 0, 1, 2, 3) sufficient to define a Jacobian J(Q), namely the complex torus built from the homology in the middle dimension of Q.

For an ordinary 2-dimensional conformal space (Riemann surface) Σ, let D^int_0(Σ) denote the space of integral 0-currents on Σ (formal integer linear combinations of points, i.e. integral 0-cycles, with the topology and metric induced from currents). The space D^int_0(Σ) is a quasi Riemann surface, and its Jacobian coincides with the classical Jacobian variety of Σ.

Problem. Prove or disprove: every quasi Riemann surface Q is isomorphic, as a quasi Riemann surface, to D^int_0(Σ) for some 2-dimensional conformal space Σ whose Jacobian J(Σ) is isomorphic to J(Q). If the statement holds, give an explicit construction of Σ from Q together with the isomorphism Q ≅ D^int_0(Σ).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is due to Friedan in his "Quasi Riemann surfaces" papers (2017). Friedan himself characterizes the conjecture as speculative with no supporting evidence at the time of writing. No subsequent literature appears to establish or refute it, so it remains open.

status_evidence.title: Quasi Riemann surfaces II. Questions, comments, speculations
status_evidence.snippet: every quasi Riemann surface Q is isomorphic to the quasi Riemann surface Q(Σ) associated to a unique two-dimensional conformal space Σ whose ordinary Jacobian J(Σ) is isomorphic to J(Q)
status_evidence.claim: States the conjecture; describes it as speculation without supporting evidence.

status_evidence.title: Quasi Riemann surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: prototypes of quasi-Riemann surfaces are the spaces of integral 0-currents of total mass m in a Riemann surface Σ
status_evidence.claim: Defines D^int_0(Σ) as the prototype example of quasi Riemann surfaces.
